title: model2data model
description: A data model: its tables, their columns and keys, the relationships between them, the enums a column can be typed as, and how each column's values are generated. Written as YAML (the `.model2data.yml` file) or as JSON; both are the same document. This schema is normative together with model2data/spec/README.md, which defines the YAML profile a reader must apply and the checks that depend on more than one part of the document.

model2data.description: The spec version the document is written against, `MAJOR.MINOR` or `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Write it as `0.2.0`. A reader that met the YAML number 0.2 reads it as `0.2`.

name.description: The model's name. Names the generated dbt project, normalised to `[a-z0-9_]`. Defaults to the file's name without `.model2data.yml`.

description.description: What the model is, in prose.

enums.description: The enums a column's `type` can name, keyed by enum name: `status` in the default schema, `billing.status` in another.

tables.description: The tables, keyed by table key: `orders` in the default schema, `raw.orders` in another. Generation order follows the foreign keys, not the document; everything else that lists tables uses document order.

relationships.description: Relationships that belong to no single column. Only many-to-many ones: a foreign key is written on its column (`references`) or its table (`foreign_keys`).

groups.description: Named groups of tables, for reading a large model: drawn as one box on a diagram. No effect on generation.

run.description: Generation settings saved with the model, so that a seed and a day are part of the file rather than a command line. Every setting is optional; a reader's own options (CLI flags, the studio's settings) override them.

name.description: A name: at least one character, no `.`, no path separator, no control character, at most 200 characters.

qualifiedName.description: `name` or `schema.name`: one or two names joined by a single `.`.

columnPath.description: A column of a table: `table.column` or `schema.table.column`. The last `.` separates the column from the table key.

color.description: A hex colour literal: `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`. Quote it in YAML, where `#` starts a comment.

enum.description: An enum's members, in order: a list of values, or a mapping of value to a description of it (null for none).

enumValue.description: An enum member. An integer member is the member whose text is its decimal form.

description.description: What one row of the table is, in prose. Becomes the dbt model's description.

color.description: The table's header colour on a diagram; lines into the table take it too.

role.description: The table's role when a star schema or a Data Vault is derived from the model, overriding the inferred one. `fact`: events or measurements. `dimension`: an entity described. A bridge is only ever inferred.

columns.description: The table's columns, keyed by name, in the order they are generated and exported. A column written as a plain string is a column of that type and nothing else: `country: country`.

keys.description: Keys over more than one column. A key on one column is written on the column (`pk`, `unique`).

foreign_keys.description: Foreign keys over more than one column. A foreign key of one column is written on the column (`references`).

type.description: The column's type. An SQL type (`bigint`, `numeric(10,2)`, `timestamp`, `text[]`), the name of an enum in the model, or the name of a generator (`email`, `first_name`, `ean13`): a generator type exports as the SQL type the generator's values have. Matched case-insensitively.

pk.description: The column is the table's primary key. Implies `not_null` and `unique`. More than one `pk` column in a table form one composite primary key, as if listed under `keys`.

unique.description: No two rows hold the same value.

not_null.description: No row holds null. Without it a column is nullable, and some of its rows are generated null: see `generate.null_rate`.

increment.description: The column is auto-incremented by the database. Documentation for the exported DDL; the generator does not read it.

default.description: The column's static default value. A row generated null holds this value instead. An expression default (`now()`) is not a static value and is written as `x-default-expression`.

description.description: What the column holds, in prose. Becomes the dbt column's description.

references.description: The column is a foreign key onto this column of another (or the same) table, which should be the parent's primary key or unique: onto any other column it is a warning, not an error, and every non-null child value is drawn from the values that column holds (see the README, References). Many-to-one unless `one_to_one` is set.

one_to_one.description: At most one child row per parent row.

measure.description: Whether the column is a measure (a value to sum or average) when a star schema or a Data Vault is derived from the model, overriding the inferred answer.

x-default-expression.description: An SQL expression default, kept for the exported DDL. Not generated.

key.description: A key over several columns of the table: `{pk: [a, b]}` or `{unique: [a, b]}`. Each member of a `pk` key is not null.

foreignKey.description: A foreign key over several columns: `columns` of this table reference `to_columns` of `references`, pairwise.

relationship.description: A many-to-many relationship between two columns. Drawn and documented; generates nothing, since no table holds its key. Model a join table to generate one.

generate.description: How the column's values are generated. Every hint is optional; one left out means the generator's default for the column. Which hints a column may carry depends on its kind: see `x-model2data-applies-to` on each, and the kinds in the spec README.

min.description: The lowest value generated. Without a `distribution` (or with `uniform`), values are drawn evenly between `min` and `max`, both inclusive; with any other distribution, draws below `min` are redrawn up to 20 times and then clamped to it. A bound left out takes the column's default range: 0 to 100 on an integer column, 0 to 10,000 on a decimal one. On an integer column it must be an integer, and with the other bound resolved it must not exceed `max`. Decimal values are rounded to 2 places, integer ones to the nearest integer.

max.description: The highest value generated; the mirror of `min`, with the same default range, rounding and clamping.

distribution.description: The shape numeric values are drawn from: a kind alone (`lognormal`), whose parameters are then derived from the range, or the kind with its parameters. A parameter left out is derived from the range (explicit `min`/`max`, else the column's default range): normal `mean` is its midpoint and `stddev` a sixth of its width; lognormal `median` is its midpoint and `spread` 0.5; exponential `mean` is its midpoint. Only an explicit `min`/`max` clips the draws.

mean.description: The centre of the bell curve.

median.description: The typical value, exp(μ) of the underlying normal.

spread.description: σ of the underlying normal: how heavy the tail is (0.3 mild, 1.0 heavy).

null_rate.description: The fraction of rows generated null (or the column's `default`, when it has one): exactly ⌊n × null_rate⌋ of n rows. Replaces the default rate, which is min(0.2, 1 − n / (n + 50)).

weights.description: The relative weight of each enum member, drawn in proportion. A member left out weighs 1. Every key must be a member of the column's enum.

true_rate.description: The probability each generated value is true. Without it, a fair coin. Nulls are applied afterwards, so this is the share of true among non-null values.

distinct.description: Generate a pool of this many values, by the column's own type and its other hints, then draw every row from the pool with replacement, so the column behaves like a category.

skew.description: How unevenly the foreign key's values spread over the parent rows, replacing the run's skew for this column. 0: every parent equally likely. Above 0: the parents, in a seeded random order, are weighted exp(−8 · skew² · i / n) by rank i of n; at 0.8 the top fifth of parents hold roughly 65–75% of the rows, at 1.0 roughly 80%.

after.description: Another temporal column of the same table. In every row, this column's value is not earlier than that column's. The `after` hints of one table must not form a cycle.

business_hours.description: Replaces the run's business-hours setting for this column. When true, weekend days weigh 0.3 against a weekday's 1, and a timestamp's hour is drawn from a working-day profile (busiest 08:00–17:59, a lunch dip, rare at night) rather than evenly.

growth.description: Replaces the run's growth for this column. A day at fraction t through the generated window (0 at its start, 1 at its end) weighs 1 + growth · t: 0 is flat, 1 makes the end twice as busy as the start, −1 tails off to nothing.

seasonality.description: Replaces the run's seasonality for this column. A day weighs 1 + seasonality · cos(2π (d − 320) / 365.25), d its day of the year: an annual peak on 16 November. 0 is no seasonal pattern; 1 the strongest.

rows_per_table.description: Row counts for individual tables, keyed by table key, overriding `rows`.

seed.description: Makes the run reproducible: the same seed, model, settings, `as_of` and engine version produce the same bytes.

table_seeds.description: Re-rolls single tables, keyed by table key: a table's values change with its entry, every other table's stay byte-identical. Needs `seed`.

as_of.description: The day every generated date and timestamp is placed relative to: dates fall in the two years up to it, timestamps in the year up to it. An ISO 8601 date. Without it, today.

locale.description: The locale people and addresses are drawn from, as `ll_CC`: `en_US`, `nl_BE`.

shape.description: The run's defaults for the temporal and foreign-key hints of the same names, applied to every column that does not set its own.
